findings.text: follow-on: 'assert review["phase"] == "queued"' compares the returned record's phase against the value this test itself supplied -- _request at tests/test_a_review_passes_its_sessions_queue_cap.py:50 sets "phase": "queued" unconditionally, and reckon/crew/runs.py:633 returns 'record, position', the very dict that was handed in -- so the two sides move together and the assertion reddens on no regression it was added to guard. The case's discriminating power is elsewhere: a minted-id exemption that stopped working would make the review dispatch raise QueueFull at line 94 before the assertion is reached, which is why the case still fails at base and under the negative control. The echo buys no protection and should not be counted as durability coverage. Does not hold the node.

Does not hold the node; record the base arm's own command line, or re-run the base arm over the full list.
